title: Check yourself: Sensitive talk, hand-offs and judging a conversation

questions.stem: In a reviewed batch of 200 conversations, 199 are excellent, and one customer's message about their own safety got a product tip. The average quality score is 98. What does the review decide?

options.text: Ship it on the strength of an average that clears any reasonable bar by a wide margin
options.says: Ruled out because the average is not the test: "A safety miss is not averaged: one missed signal holds the release however good the rest is."

options.text: Hold it until such cases are routed to a person every time
options.says: A missed signal holds the release.

options.text: Ship it with a note that one case in two hundred is within normal noise
options.says: Ruled out because the safety count has no noise allowance: "the review has one number that is never averaged and several that are".

options.text: Hold it only if the next batch shows a second case of the same kind
options.says: Ruled out because one case is enough: "A safety miss is not averaged: one missed signal holds the release however good the rest is."

questions.stem: A conversation is handed over after a signal of risk. What should the assistant do while the person takes over?

options.text: Keep the conversation going as usual until the person arrives
options.says: Ruled out because the assistant does not keep chatting: "it does not diagnose, advise or keep chatting about the order".

options.text: Acknowledge the message, say that someone is coming, and stop advising
options.says: The assistant acknowledges and hands over.

options.text: Offer a diagnosis of what the customer is going through and a plan to address it
options.says: Ruled out because it does not diagnose: "it does not diagnose, advise or keep chatting about the order".

options.text: Finish the order question first, then mention that a person may join afterwards
options.says: Ruled out because the order question does not come first: "it does not diagnose, advise or keep chatting about the order".

origin.section: Sensitive talk is routed, not prompted

questions.stem: A policy allows at most 10 percent repeated questions. A batch of 20 conversations has 2 of them. Does the batch pass that check?

options.text: No, because any repeated question counts against the assistant in a review
options.says: Ruled out because the policy allows some: "A limit is met at the limit, so exactly ten percent repeated questions pass and twenty do not."

options.text: No, because the limit has to be stayed under and cannot simply be touched
options.says: Ruled out for the same reason: "A limit is met at the limit, so exactly ten percent repeated questions pass and twenty do not."

options.text: Yes, since the share equals the limit and a limit is met when reached
options.says: Two of twenty is exactly ten percent.

options.text: Yes, since the repeats all came from a single customer in the batch
options.says: Ruled out because the source of the repeats plays no part: "The share of conversations in which the assistant asked the same question twice."
